claims.statement: Administrative writing increased capacity to classify, aggregate and audit labor, goods and obligations when tied to institutional procedure.
claims.counterevidence: Records alone do not prove compliance or causal primacy.
claims.narrative_implication: Use only with the stated confidence and boundary.

claims.statement: Ur III labor records reveal ordinary people mainly through top-down categories and required work.
claims.counterevidence: They do not recover the full lives or viewpoints of recorded workers.
claims.narrative_implication: Use only with the stated confidence and boundary.

claims.statement: Writing’s power distribution changed over time: uses once concentrated in royal/institutional systems were later appropriated by urban private actors.
claims.counterevidence: The scale and timing of ‘privatization’ vary by region.
claims.narrative_implication: Use only with the stated confidence and boundary.

claims.statement: A written law, norm or transaction is evidence of recording and claim-making, not automatic evidence of enforcement.
claims.counterevidence: Case-specific links among tablet, witnesses, seal and action are required.
claims.narrative_implication: Use only with the stated confidence and boundary.

claims.statement: Archive survival is structurally biased by clay durability, institutional discard, excavation history and antiquities-market provenance.
claims.counterevidence: Bias does not invalidate the corpus, but limits population-wide inference.
claims.narrative_implication: Use only with the stated confidence and boundary.

claims.statement: At Puzriš-Dagan, more than 13,500 tablets reconstruct an archival agency tied to livestock, taxation, royal gifts and diplomacy; the archive should not be read as a literal inventory of one stockyard.
claims.counterevidence: The surviving repository is selective and its reconstructed units remain scholarly models.
claims.narrative_implication: Use as a bounded causal case in which records, seals, officials and retrieval practices jointly made obligations actionable.

claims.statement: Agency belongs to people and institutions using records: tablets stabilize classifications, scribes and sealers authenticate them, archives make them retrievable, and authorities supply enforcement.
claims.counterevidence: The strength of each link differs by archive; a preserved record alone cannot demonstrate enforcement.
claims.narrative_implication: Never say writing itself commanded, owned or coerced.

claims.statement: Distributional effects were asymmetric: record systems improved institutional visibility and elite/private claims while exposing workers and dependents through imposed categories.
claims.counterevidence: People could also use documents strategically, and private uptake widened access in some later settings.
claims.narrative_implication: Pair every capacity gain with who gained legibility, leverage, burden or exclusion.

claims.statement: Oral negotiation, embodied skill, household practice and much routine exchange remained partly or wholly outside surviving writing.
claims.counterevidence: Absence from archives cannot quantify the size of unwritten domains.
claims.narrative_implication: State the limit; do not turn archival silence into proof of absence.
